minutes.headline: Commissioners move to fine and force removal of kayak racks illegally stored in the water supply protection zone
minutes.summary: The Board of Water Commissioners voted to move ahead with fines and possible forced removal to make the Woodlands take kayak racks out of the water supply protection zone, after months of the association's lawyer stalling. Commissioners also reviewed quotes for a new excavator to replace aging equipment, heard how much the district saved doing the Rolling Acres water main project in-house, and approved upgrading the district's billing software to better track backflow testing.

votes.motion: Give all employees a one-time bonus for completing the Rolling Acres project
Spend $3,500 to update the backflow testing service-management program in NDS

budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent presented quotes for a rubber-tired excavator to replace aging backhoe equipment, citing a budget figure well below a larger, costlier machine class. Commissioners debated narrowing the spec before deciding whether to go out to bid.

budget_items.topic: Rolling Acres water main project: in-house cost vs. contractor estimate
budget_items.what_was_said: The superintendent estimated what it cost the district to do the main replacement itself versus hiring an outside excavating firm plus engineering, and said the district saved a substantial amount by doing the work in-house.

budget_items.topic: One-time employee bonus for Rolling Acres project
budget_items.what_was_said: A commissioner proposed a one-time bonus for every employee, including office staff, in recognition of completing the Rolling Acres project without an outside contractor.
The district reported signing documents for another PFAS settlement payment and estimated the running total of settlement money received, noting it goes into surplus rather than a specific fund.

budget_items.topic: NDS billing system upgrade for backflow tracking
budget_items.what_was_said: Staff requested funding to add a service-management module to the district's existing NDS billing software to track backflow tests, describing it as a first step toward a fuller work-order system.
Staff described the current per-test and additional-test backflow fee as context for whether the new tracking system would pay for itself.

decisions.decision: Staff will contact the district's attorney (KP) to draft a letter to the Woodlands imposing fines over the kayak racks remaining in the water protection zone.
Fines on the Woodlands for the kayak racks will begin immediately, with removal by an outside contractor if the racks are not gone within 30 days.
The attorney's draft letter will be emailed to each commissioner individually for approval rather than reviewed together at a meeting.
The superintendent will narrow down the exact excavator specification before the district decides how to bid or purchase, possibly waiting on the water tower pilot test or a special meeting.
The district will proceed with the NDS backflow-tracking add-on for now but keep looking into switching to a more comprehensive billing/work-order platform later.
Staff will ask the district's own attorney whether the kayak-rack letter should also go to the Woodlands' attorney, and consider sending it certified.

what_happened.line: Commissioners voted to pursue fines and possible forced removal of kayak racks the Woodlands has kept in the water supply protection zone.
The district's attorney will draft a fine letter to the Woodlands, to be circulated to commissioners by email rather than reviewed at a meeting.
Commissioners approved an expenditure to add backflow-testing tracking to the district's existing billing software.
A proposed one-time bonus for all employees over the in-house Rolling Acres water main project was not audible in the recording.
The superintendent will narrow the specification for a replacement excavator before the district decides how to purchase it.

why_it_matters: Enforcement in the water supply protection zone concerns land use rules meant to protect the town's drinking water source, and could mean costs or a forced cleanup for the Woodlands association.
The billing software purchase is public money spent on tracking backflow test compliance, a water-safety requirement for connected properties.
The excavator decision, still undecided, will shape a future equipment purchase or bid the district brings back to the board.
